# simpleconf

> simpleconf is a configuration server that holds a single JSON document and lets clients read and write paths inside it, such as `product.name`, over HTTP or a line-based TCP protocol. Writes go to an append-only file. Several nodes can run as a Raft cluster.

It is written in Go, MIT licensed, and ships as one binary or the `shonhen/simpleconf` Docker image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64). It is meant for the small, shared settings a handful of services read often and change occasionally: feature flags, endpoints, limits.

Use etcd or Consul instead if you need watches on keys, per-key access control, TLS, or data that does not comfortably fit in memory. simpleconf has none of those, and no authentication: keep its ports on a private network or put a proxy in front.

Quick start:

```bash
docker run -p 23456:23456 -v simpleconf-data:/data shonhen/simpleconf
curl -X PUT localhost:23456/db/product.name -d '"Demo"'
curl localhost:23456/db/product          # {"name":"Demo"}
```

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shaunlee/simpleconf/main/README.md): quick start, key paths and gjson queries, HTTP API, TCP protocol, configuration, durability and fsync modes, Raft cluster, peers mode
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shaunlee/simpleconf/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): read and write paths, Raft and peers modes, node-to-node protocols
- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shaunlee/simpleconf/main/docs/benchmarks.md): setup, caveats and full tables, including comparisons with etcd, Consul and Valkey
